name: Salt-water / sodium bicarbonate claims

lead: These are low-cost household routines: baking soda as a mild abrasive or supplement and salt water as a rinse or cleanser.
People use them for cleaner-feeling skin and teeth and, with baking soda, to support training endurance.

paras: Baking soda is a mild alkaline abrasive that neutralises acid; ingested, it buffers acid during intense exercise.
It irritates eyes, and large intakes can cause alkalosis. Claims that it treats cancer have drawn a warning from the American Cancer Society.

web.title: ISSN position stand: sodium bicarbonate and exercise performance

chain: Baking soda acts as a mild abrasive and acid neutraliser; salt water as a rinse
Used on teeth, skin or in the mouth
Cleaner-feeling teeth and skin; with pre-training use, more work capacity in hard sets
angle.text: People use baking soda and salt water as low-cost cleansers and scrubs for skin and teeth, aiming for a cleaner, fresher look. Baking soda is also taken before intense training, where it is studied for muscular endurance and so indirectly for physique.

lead: Salt-water and sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) routines are inexpensive household practices that people fold into grooming and training to look cleaner and, through training capacity, more muscular. Baking soda is used as a mild abrasive and acid-neutralising ingredient for teeth and mouth, in homemade deodorants and as a gentle scrub, while salt water is used as a rinse or cleanser [1][1]. Taken before hard sessions, baking soda is also a sports supplement aimed at muscular endurance [1][2].

Sodium bicarbonate is described as a mechanical cleanser for teeth and gums and an acid neutraliser in mouthwashes, and a dilute solution has been used for lash-line hygiene in blepharitis [1]. Salt-based cleansing products also exist commercially; a Chinese patent from 2007 describes a face-washing mask built mainly on mineral salts [3].

The International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand reports that bicarbonate benefits muscular endurance tasks, several combat sports and high-intensity cycling, running, swimming and rowing, with effects greatest in efforts lasting roughly 30 seconds to 12 minutes [2]. For skin and teeth routines, no trials of these household uses as cosmetic methods have been published.
infobox: Sodium bicarbonate, table or sea salt
Mouth rinse, scrub, deodorant, sports supplement

paras: Sodium bicarbonate is used in mouthwashes as a gentle abrasive and acid neutraliser, as an antacid, and as a deodorant ingredient, either dry or mixed into a paste [1]. A paste of baking soda and water has been used on insect bites and stings [1]. For eyelid hygiene in blepharitis, a teaspoon dissolved in cooled boiled water has been described for cleaning the base of the lashes [1].

Salt water is used as a rinse for the mouth and as a cleanser, and mineral-salt face masks have been patented [3]. Pink and Himalayan salts are also marketed for spa wall linings, salt lamps and inhalation treatments, which Wikipedia notes are promoted with health claims that lack scientific support [4].

Baking soda is taken to buffer acid produced in hard exercise. The ISSN position stand concludes that benefit is seen in muscular endurance, combat sports (boxing, judo, karate, taekwondo, wrestling) and high-intensity cycling, running, swimming and rowing, in men and women, with very brief single efforts and long low-intensity exercise less likely to benefit [2].

The stand reports that part of the effect appears placebo-driven, and that bloating, nausea, vomiting and abdominal pain are the most common side effects, varying between individuals [2]. Wikipedia likewise says studies, mostly in males, suggest the greatest help in short-term high-intensity activity [1].

Sodium bicarbonate is classified as causing serious eye irritation, and excess intake can cause alkalosis [1]. The American Cancer Society has warned against its use as a cancer treatment, citing unproven effectiveness and potential harm [1]. Sports use can cause gastrointestinal symptoms [2].

Salt appears in training and diet threads mostly in relation to water retention: one T Nation poster describes taking a week to purge bloating after a very high-salt, high-calorie meal [5], and another says they eat about ten times the recommended salt per day [6]. Discussion of baking soda as a face or teeth scrub is rare in the sources reviewed.
No studies found for salt-water or baking-soda facial or tooth routines as cosmetic methods.

Related research covers sodium bicarbonate as an exercise supplement [2], and a 2026 single-arm trial of daily saturated saline immersion in 17 participants with refractory plantar warts [7]. A 2025 randomised study compared warm saltwater and warm water baths in rheumatoid arthritis for pain, fatigue and sleep [8]. These studied other outcomes.

lore.intro: Community discussion of salt and bicarbonate is mostly in passing, in training logs and diet threads where salt intake, bloating and water retention come up [5][6].
